_comment: AOS Sprint 23 — Engagement Templates. Structured, faithful extraction of templates/proposals/*.md's own already-authored content (challengeFraming, keyDeliverables) so Sales Director's executive_proposal_document() can reuse this real IP directly instead of only citing the filename. Nothing here is invented — every field is drawn verbatim (or near-verbatim, trimmed) from the matching .md file's own 'Understanding the Challenge' and 'Deliverables' sections. Keyed by the exact filename service-mapping/runtime/generate.py's determine_proposal_template() already selects (service-catalogue.json's proposalTemplateByDomainTag/proposalTemplateByPrimaryService) — never a second, independent selection rule. Edit the .md files first if the underlying pitch changes; keep this file in sync by hand.

ai-governance-proposal-template.md.challengeFraming: {{CLIENT_NAME}} is deploying or planning to deploy AI capabilities where governance has not kept pace with adoption: {{SPECIFIC_CONTEXT, e.g. "no named owner per use case," "no consistent risk evaluation across use cases," "policy exists but is not operational"}}. The gap is rarely the framework; it is translating an AI governance intent into ownership, evidence and an operating rhythm that holds up under board and regulatory scrutiny.
keyDeliverables: AI Use-Case Inventory and Risk Register
RACI Matrix for AI governance decisions
Decision Framework covering risk evaluation and approval gates
Governance Charter
Board Reporting Pack

dora-proposal-template.md.challengeFraming: {{CLIENT_NAME}} needs to demonstrate digital operational resilience under DORA, specifically around {{SPECIFIC_CONTEXT, e.g. "ICT third-party risk management," "incident reporting readiness," "resilience testing obligations"}}. DORA changes what monitoring has to mean for ICT third parties: a vendor compliant at onboarding can drift out of alignment as the obligation itself evolves, with no commercial breach involved.
keyDeliverables: Risk Register: DORA readiness gap assessment, Likelihood/Impact/Risk Rating scored per critical ICT third party
Operating Model for ICT third-party governance
Evidence Register for ongoing monitoring and incident reporting
Board Reporting Pack

enterprise-consulting-proposal-template..challengeFraming: {{CLIENT_NAME}} needs a broader governance engagement spanning {{SPECIFIC_CONTEXT, e.g. "multiple domains: AI governance, technology risk and third-party governance together," "an enterprise-wide operating model, not a single-domain fix," "coordination across several business units and committees"}}. This is scoped as a larger programme rather than a single-domain engagement.
keyDeliverables: Governance Charter covering the full programme mandate
Operating Model with decision rights across all domains in scope
RACI Matrix, Risk Register and Evidence Register per domain, rolled up to one Governance Dashboard
Implementation Roadmap, phased by risk exposure
Board Reporting Pack

iso-42001-proposal-template.md.challengeFraming: {{CLIENT_NAME}} needs to stand up or mature an AI Management System (AIMS) against ISO/IEC 42001 for {{SPECIFIC_CONTEXT, e.g. "a certification readiness assessment," "closing gaps identified in a prior internal audit," "building the AIMS from scratch ahead of a customer or regulator asking for it"}}. ISO 42001 is a management-system standard, not a technical checklist: the hard part is rarely Annex A's control list, it is the Clause 4-10 operating system around it.
keyDeliverables: AIMS Scope Statement and Applicability Statement (Annex A control applicability, with justification for any exclusion)
AI Risk Assessment and AI System Impact Assessment, Likelihood/Impact/Risk Rating scored per AI system, per Clause 6
Gap Assessment against ISO 42001 Clauses 4-10 and Annex A
Documented Information Set (AIMS policy, procedures, records templates) sufficient for an internal or certification audit
Internal Audit Programme and Management Review cadence
Board Reporting Pack

eu-ai-act-proposal-template.md.challengeFraming: {{CLIENT_NAME}} needs to operationalise the EU AI Act's risk-tiered obligations for {{SPECIFIC_CONTEXT, e.g. "a specific high-risk AI system," "an AI inventory across multiple business units," "conformity assessment preparation"}}. The Act is rarely the hard part to understand; it is translating risk-tier obligations into ownership, evidence and an operating rhythm that a regulator or notified body can actually examine.
keyDeliverables: AI Inventory classified by EU AI Act risk tier
Risk Register, Likelihood/Impact/Risk Rating scored per AI system, and technical documentation structure
RACI Matrix for AI governance decisions, with real named individuals confirmed, not titles only
Board Reporting Pack

fractional-advisory-proposal-template.md.challengeFraming: {{CLIENT_NAME}} needs senior AI and technology governance direction without a full-time hire: {{SPECIFIC_CONTEXT, e.g. "board and committee reporting on AI oversight," "ongoing risk appetite and policy decisions," "a governance function that has no senior owner yet"}}. Fractional advisory gives that direction on an ongoing, part-time basis, scaled to what the organisation actually needs.
keyDeliverables: Ongoing Decision Register and Governance Dashboard
Board Reporting Pack, refreshed on the agreed cadence
RACI Matrix, updated as ownership changes

grc-proposal-template.md.challengeFraming: {{CLIENT_NAME}}'s governance operating model shows {{SPECIFIC_CONTEXT, e.g. "governance debt: duplicated committees, undocumented decisions, paper-only ownership," "a redesign that risks stalling delivery," "fragmented reporting lines"}}. A GRC transformation that tries to fix everything at once usually fixes nothing before executive sponsorship runs out; this proposal sequences by risk exposure instead.
keyDeliverables: Governance debt diagnostic
Operating Model with a target decision-rights map
Implementation Roadmap, phased by risk exposure
Governance Dashboard for effectiveness reporting

security-governance-proposal-template.md.challengeFraming: {{CLIENT_NAME}}'s cyber security programme has {{SPECIFIC_CONTEXT, e.g. "strong controls but weak governance layer above them," "no clear control ownership," "gaps discovered at assessment rather than caught in advance"}}. The governance layer behind a security programme, control ownership, gap prioritisation, assessment readiness, is usually the part that determines whether an assessment goes smoothly or becomes a scramble.
keyDeliverables: Control gap assessment against the target baseline
Risk Register: prioritised remediation roadmap
Evidence Register for assessment readiness
Board Reporting Pack

technology-risk-proposal-template.md.challengeFraming: {{CLIENT_NAME}}'s technology risk function faces {{SPECIFIC_CONTEXT, e.g. "a risk appetite statement engineers cannot apply," "a control library that does not match actual exposure," "assurance evidence reconstructed after the fact rather than maintained"}}. The objective is a risk appetite and control ownership model that holds up under audit, not a document that describes intent without changing practice.
keyDeliverables: Risk Register built from the reset taxonomy and control library
Decision Framework: risk appetite in operational language
Evidence Register for control ownership and testing
Board Reporting Pack

third-party-risk-proposal-template.md.challengeFraming: {{CLIENT_NAME}}'s third-party risk programme is {{SPECIFIC_CONTEXT, e.g. "strong at onboarding, weak at everything after," "unclear on who owns a vendor relationship once onboarding ends," "not proportional to vendor criticality"}}. The risk that actually materialises usually lives after signature, not at onboarding: a subprocessor changes, a data flow expands, a control lapses, and nothing triggers review unless someone is assigned to look for it.
keyDeliverables: Risk Register segmented by vendor criticality and data access, Likelihood/Impact/Risk Rating scored per vendor tier
Operating Model for the third-party governance framework
Evidence Register for ongoing monitoring and re-assessment
Exit and offboarding governance checklist
